meta.title: Fushi — Language Acquisition
meta.description: Fushi: a free, open-source immersion app for language learning. Tap a word while watching anime, reading, or playing games to look it up, tap again to make an Anki card with the sentence, screenshot and audio. Windows / macOS / Android / iOS.
home.hero.eyebrow: All-in-one · works out of the box
home.hero.title:
Language acquisition
should be this much fun
home.hero.copy: Minimal setup, maximum output. Player, dictionaries, lookup, card making, downloads and season tracking — what used to take a pile of tools now takes one app. Hit an unknown word while watching, reading or gaming? Tap it for the definition, tap plus, and the sentence, screenshot, audio and definition land in Anki.
home.acgn.title: What you love is the best textbook.
home.acgn.copy: No need to set aside time to “study”. Watching the shows, reading the books and playing the games you like is the study — look up and save new words on the spot, without stopping or switching apps.

home.method.p1: Download Fushi and follow the onboarding guide.
home.method.p2: Pick material you like — that is the single most important thing. Anime (first choice), visual novels or audiobooks are good places to start. Material varies in difficulty; do not force yourself through something too hard.
home.method.p3: When you hit a word you do not know, tap to look it up and make a card (skip it if the sentence is too hard or you are not in the mood). When a whole passage is unclear, try looking things up — and if it still does not click, that is fine, skip it. Learn to tolerate ambiguity: not understanding is normal, and with enough immersion it starts to make sense on its own.
home.method.p4: Learning is slow accumulation. Choose material you genuinely enjoy — interest always comes first; only what you enjoy will keep you immersing every day.
home.method.tip1: When to startYou do not need a big vocabulary before immersing. 500–1000 words is plenty — or honestly, whenever you feel like starting.
home.method.tip2: Improving listeningOnce you know around 2000–5000 words, try watching anime with subtitles hidden. It does wonders for listening.
home.method.tip3: About subtitlesUse subtitles in the target language — the same language as the video. Early on you can add native-language subtitles as a second track to help, but they are a crutch: drop them as soon as you can. With enough vocabulary, try hiding subtitles altogether.
home.closing.title:
You are already learning.
All you need is the tool.

dl.title: Download Fushi
dl.lead: Pick a platform, install it, and let the in-app onboarding handle the rest. Four platforms, one experience, all free and open source.
dl.linux: There is no prebuilt Linux package yet; please build from source.
dl.guide_p1: The first time Fushi starts it opens the onboarding guide: it asks which features you want, then sets up the recommended dictionary pack, Anki, backup sync and reading fonts step by step. Closed it and want to run it again? Go to Settings → System → Onboarding.
dl.guide_r1_b: Choose the interface language and light/dark theme
dl.guide_r2_b: Untick the modules you do not need; they disappear from the bottom bar
dl.guide_r3_b: Download and import Japanese dictionaries plus Japanese/English pronunciation audio
dl.guide_r4_b: Connect AnkiDroid / AnkiConnect and create the Lapis deck in one tap
dl.guide_r5_b: Optional — all of these can be skipped
dl.pack_p1: The pack contains Japanese vocabulary, pitch-accent and frequency dictionaries plus local Japanese / English pronunciation audio, about 9.5 GB. Download and import it right from the “Install recommended pack” step of the guide — chunked, parallel, multi-mirror and resumable, no link hunting required.
dl.pack_warn_title: Do this on a fresh install
dl.pack_warn_body: Importing the pack goes through the backup-restore flow and overwrites existing local data. The best time is right after installing, before you import your own books and videos.
dl.pack_p2: Learning another language? Skip this step and import any Yomitan / MDX (MDict) / DSL / Migaku dictionary through dictionary management. The languages you can look up depend on the dictionaries you import, not on the interface language.
dl.anki_p1: Anki — the name comes from the Japanese 暗記 (anki, memorisation) — is the most widely used spaced-repetition (SRS) software in the world. Words you look up in Fushi go into Anki with one tap, giving you the best retention for the least review time. Install it first from the Anki website.
dl.anki_tip_body: Anki's default algorithm is SM2 from over 30 years ago and performs poorly. In the deck options, switch to the built-in FSRS — one of the best spaced-repetition algorithms available.
dl.anki_p2: The Anki step of the guide walks you through the steps below. To set it up manually or later, go to Settings → Card making.
dl.anki_android_2: Back in Fushi, go to Settings → Card making.
dl.anki_android_3: Tap “Refresh decks and note types” (① in the screenshot); Fushi asks for permission — allow it.
dl.anki_android_4: Tap “Create Lapis deck” (② in the screenshot).
dl.anki_android_5: No red warnings or errors means you are set.
dl.anki_windows_2: Open the Tools menu in the top-left → Add-ons → Get Add-ons.
dl.anki_windows_3: Paste the add-on code to install AnkiConnect: 2055492159, then restart Anki.
dl.anki_windows_4: Back in Fushi, go to Settings → Card making.
dl.anki_windows_5: Click “Refresh decks and note types” (① in the screenshot).
dl.anki_windows_6: Click “Create Lapis deck” (② in the screenshot).
dl.anki_windows_7: No red warnings or errors means you are set.
dl.anki_p3: Once that is done, take a look around the settings: reading theme, fonts, furigana and interface scale can all be tuned to taste — though the defaults work fine too.
dl.immerse_title: Skip the word lists — start with immersion
dl.immerse_p1: Pick material you like — that is the single most important thing. Anime (first choice), visual novels or audiobooks are good places to start. Material varies in difficulty; do not force yourself through something too hard.

When a whole passage is unclear, try looking things up — and if it still does not click, that is fine, skip it. Learn to tolerate ambiguity: not understanding is normal, and with enough immersion it starts to make sense on its own.

dl.tip_listening_body: Once you know around 2000–5000 words, try watching anime with subtitles hidden. It does wonders for listening.

dl.closing_p1: Import an EPUB, drop in an episode, or search and download right inside the app — and whenever you meet a word you do not know, tap once to look it up and once more to remember it.
dl.closing_p2: Questions? Ask on Discord or in the QQ group — feedback is handled quickly. Full guides in more languages: Simplified Chinese (Feishu) and the English Guide.
